scenes.title: The Island of Aeolus
scenes.summary: Odysseus' tale goes on. They come to the floating island of Aeolus, son of Hippotes, walled with bronze, where he lives feasting with his wife and their six sons and six daughters, whom he has married to one another. For a month he entertains Odysseus and asks him about Troy and the homecoming of the Achaeans; then, as dispenser of the winds, he gives him an oxhide skin in which he has bound the winds, ties it in the ship with a silver cord, and lets only the West Wind blow.

scenes.title: The Skin of the Winds
scenes.summary: For nine days they sail day and night, and on the tenth Ithaca is in sight and they can see men tending fires. Odysseus, worn out from handling the sheet himself, falls asleep, and his companions, sure that the skin holds gold and silver that Aeolus gave him alone, open it; the winds rush out and the storm drives them back to the Aeolian island. Odysseus wakes and debates whether to throw himself into the sea, but endures, lying covered in the ship.

scenes.title: Aeolus Sends Them Away
scenes.summary: Odysseus goes with a herald and a companion to the house of Aeolus and sits on the threshold, blaming his companions and sleep. Aeolus drives him from the island: it is not right to help a man hated by the gods. They row on in despair, with no wind to carry them.

scenes.title: The Laestrygonians
scenes.summary: On the seventh day they reach Telepylus, the city of Lamus, where the paths of night and day are close together. The other ships moor in the enclosed harbor; Odysseus keeps his outside. His scouts meet the king's daughter at the spring Artacia and find her mother, as huge as a mountain, who calls Antiphates; he seizes one of them for his meal. The Laestrygonians, like Giants, smash the ships with rocks from the cliffs and spear the men like fish. Odysseus cuts his cable and his ship alone escapes.

scenes.title: Aeaea
scenes.summary: They come to Aeaea, the island of Circe, sister of Aeetes and daughter of the Sun, and lie two days on the shore in grief. On the third Odysseus climbs a lookout and sees smoke from Circe's house; on his way back a god sends a great stag across his path, which he kills and carries to the ship, and they feast until sunset. At dawn he tells his companions of the smoke in the middle of the island, and they weep, remembering the Laestrygonians and the Cyclops.

scenes.title: Circe's House
scenes.summary: Odysseus divides the men into two bands, and the lot falls on Eurylochus' band. In the glens they find Circe's house of polished stone, with wolves and lions around it, bewitched by her drugs, fawning like dogs. They hear her singing at her loom, and Polites bids them call; she invites them in, all but Eurylochus, who suspects a trick, gives them cheese, barley meal and honey in Pramnian wine mixed with drugs, strikes them with her wand and pens them in her sties as swine, with their minds unchanged.

scenes.title: Eurylochus' Report
scenes.summary: Eurylochus runs back to the ship and, when he can speak, tells how the companions vanished into the house. Odysseus takes his sword and bow and orders him to lead the way; Eurylochus clasps his knees and begs to flee, and Odysseus leaves him at the ship and goes alone.

scenes.title: Hermes and the Moly
scenes.summary: On the way Hermes meets him in the likeness of a young man, tells him that his companions are penned like swine and that he too will stay there, and gives him a drug against Circe's: when she strikes him with her wand he must draw his sword as if to kill her, accept her bed, and make her swear the great oath of the gods. Hermes pulls the plant from the ground, black at the root, with a flower like milk: the gods call it moly.

scenes.title: Circe Overcome
scenes.summary: Circe gives Odysseus her mixed drink in a golden cup and strikes him with her wand, but he is not bewitched; he draws his sword and she falls at his knees, asks who he is, and knows him for Odysseus, whose coming Hermes had foretold. She invites him to her bed; he makes her swear first that she will plan no other harm against him, and then goes up into her bed.

scenes.title: The Companions Restored
scenes.summary: Circe's four handmaids, daughters of springs, groves and rivers, prepare the chairs, the tables, the wine and the bath; Odysseus is bathed and dressed but will not eat while his companions are swine. Circe lets them out of the sty and anoints each with another drug; they become men again, younger, taller and handsomer than before, and weep with Odysseus, and even the goddess pities them.

scenes.title: The Crew at Circe's House
scenes.summary: Circe sends Odysseus to bring the rest of the crew. They crowd around him like calves around their mothers; he tells them to beach the ship and follow. Eurylochus alone holds back, calling the venture as reckless as the visit to the Cyclops, and Odysseus is about to cut off his head, kinsman though he is, when the others restrain him. All go up, and Circe bids them eat and drink until their spirit returns.

scenes.title: A Year with Circe
scenes.summary: For a full year they feast. When the seasons have come round, the companions remind Odysseus of home. That night he begs Circe to send him home; she tells him he must first go to the house of Hades and Persephone to consult the soul of Teiresias, the blind Theban seer, who alone among the dead keeps his mind. Odysseus weeps and asks who will guide them, for no one has reached Hades in a black ship.

scenes.title: Circe's Instructions
scenes.summary: Circe tells him to set sail and let the North Wind carry him across Oceanus to the groves of Persephone, where Pyriphlegethon and Cocytus flow into Acheron. There he must dig a pit, pour offerings of honey and milk, wine and water, sprinkle barley meal, vow sacrifices to the dead and to Teiresias, slaughter a ram and a black ewe, and keep the other shades from the blood with his sword until Teiresias comes to tell him the way home.

scenes.title: Elpenor and the Departure
scenes.summary: At dawn Circe dresses him, and he rouses his companions. Elpenor, the youngest, who had slept on the roof drunk to keep cool, wakes at the noise, forgets the ladder, falls and breaks his neck. Odysseus tells the others where they must go, and they weep and tear their hair; at the ship they find that Circe has passed them unseen and left a ram and a black ewe.

days.label: Night of Day 33
days.note: Odysseus' tale goes on at the evening feast in the house of Alcinous (9.1–566); it runs through Books 9–12 and into the night (11.330–384). The days of the tale belong to his wanderings after Troy: a month with Aeolus, ten days at sea, a year with Circe.
